What it does: Pulls the latest data from TryBooking's S3 storage and rebuilds the local data warehouse that the dashboard and all reports read from.
Output / Recipients: Updates the dashboard automatically. No email sent.
How to run: python3 prepare_data.py - DuckDB only: python3 prepare_data.py --materialise-only
Technical notes: Builds SQLite (warehouse.db) and DuckDB (warehouse_duck.db). Runs weekends too - critical for month-end capture. Curls /api/warm after materialise. duckdb must be on PATH.

What it does: Copies TryBooking's raw data files from S3 into SharePoint so the team can access them directly.
Output / Recipients: SharePoint - Platform Data/Dashboard Data folder
How to run: python3 s3_to_sharepoint.py - preview without uploading: add --dry-run
Technical notes: ETag-based sync - only uploads changed files. Manifest at /root/s3reporting/.sync_manifest.

What it does: Keeps the Industry field in Zoho CRM up to date with the latest data from TryBooking.
Output / Recipients: Zoho CRM (field updates only - no email)
How to run: python3 zoho_industry.py
Technical notes: OAuth2 refresh token flow. Mon-Fri only.

What it does: Recalculates which tier every account belongs to and updates Zoho CRM. Also updates the retention priority score used in the dashboard.
Output / Recipients: Zoho CRM (tier fields); CSV saved to reports/; dashboard updated by 03:30
How to run: python3 zoho_tiers.py
Technical notes: Tier v2: 55% current 12m revenue + 35% lifetime + 10% years loyalty. Bands: T1 top 2%, T2 3-10%, T3 11-25%, T4 26-50%, T5 51-100%. Writes retention_priority to SQLite then triggers a second DuckDB materialise at 03:30.

What it does: Joins the TryBooking Users and Accounts S3 snapshots into one spreadsheet - one row per active user with their account's name, industry and sub-industry.
Output / Recipients: SharePoint - Platform Data/Users and Accounts/users_accounts.csv (overwrites in place)
How to run: python3 users_accounts_report.py - also save a local copy: --out /tmp/ua.csv
Technical notes: Upload-only: builds in memory and uploads, no local PII copy left on the Pi unless --out is given. Reads the monthly Users + Accounts S3 snapshots, so timing isn't sensitive.

What it does: Backs up the Pi's databases and config files to SharePoint every night in case of hardware failure. All files are encrypted before upload.
Output / Recipients: SharePoint - Backups/pi/YYYY-MM-DD/ (keeps last 7 days); every file stored encrypted as <name>.enc
How to run: python3 backup_to_sharepoint.py - skip databases: --no-warehouse - preview: --dry-run
Technical notes: Runs after the 03:30 materialise so the backup includes same-day data. Encrypts each file (streaming, bounded memory) with the key in /root/secrets/backup.key (BACKUP_SECRET_PASSPHRASE) - lose that key and backups are unrecoverable; a copy lives in the password manager. Restore with restore_from_sharepoint.py.

What it does: Sends a summary of the week's Zoho SalesIQ chat activity to the team.
Output / Recipients: Email to stakeholders
How to run: python3 salesiq_weekly.py
Technical notes: Pulls from Zoho SalesIQ API. Email via Azure Graph API. Runs 5 minutes before the accounts report.

What it does: Sends a report on new accounts signed up that week with year-on-year comparisons.
Output / Recipients: Email to stakeholders; CSV saved to reports/
How to run: python3 weekly_reporting_unified.py - to test without sending: export TEST_MODE=1 first
Technical notes: TEST_MODE redirects email to test recipients. TEST_DATE overrides the processing date. Email via Azure Graph API (Mailgun fallback).

What it does: Calculates monthly sales commissions for each salesperson based on accounts they claimed in Zoho whose first paid event has completed, and emails each person their own report.
When it runs: Monthly on the 2nd at 06:00 (reports the previous month)
Output / Recipients: PDF to each salesperson (sent to their Zoho login email); CSV summary to whoever manages commissions; CSVs saved to reports/
How to run: For previous month: export SCHEDULED_RUN=true then python3 sales_commission_report.py. Test: export TEST_MODE=1 first.
Technical notes: Runs on the 2nd so the prior month's S3 BookingData has finalised. Rates per person in sales_commission_config.json (rates only, no emails). Salesperson emails resolved from Zoho (Claimed user -> Zoho login email); needs ZohoCRM.users.READ scope. Email via Azure Graph API.

What it does: Generates detailed planning metrics - useful for target-setting, seasonality analysis, and year-end reviews. Covers revenue, cohorts, geography, industry, and keywords.
Output / Recipients: CSVs saved to planning/ seasonality/ industry/ cohorts/ geography/ keywords/
How to run: python3 eoy_planning_report.py - choose a mode: rolling / monthly_review / custom (set start+end dates)
Technical notes: Multiple output modes for different planning contexts. Requires GA4 credentials.

What it does: Breaks down accounts and revenue by industry - useful for sector-level reporting or presentations.
Output / Recipients: CSVs: industry_analysis_*.csv, industry_period_*.csv, industry_account_*.csv
How to run: python3 industry_analysis.py
Technical notes: Reads BookingDataAll + BookingData + Accounts from S3.

What it does: Pulls a full year of monthly SalesIQ chat statistics - useful for annual reviews.
Output / Recipients: CSV: salesiq_monthly_YYYY.csv
How to run: python3 salesiq_monthly_report.py - to choose a year: export YEAR=2025 first
Technical notes: Different from the weekly report - this is for historical analysis across a full year.

What it does: Matches PPC ad clicks in Google Analytics with TryBooking sign-ups to show which campaigns are converting.
Output / Recipients: CSV saved to reports/
How to run: python3 ppc_reporting.py - to test: export TEST_MODE=1 first. Campaign config: config/ppc_campaigns.json
Technical notes: Data runs from 2024-06-01 to today. Requires GA4_PROPERTY_ID and GA4_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY.

What it does: Shows the regional distribution of accounts and events across the UK based on postcodes.
Output / Recipients: CSVs: account_regional_report_*.csv, event_regional_report_*.csv
How to run: python3 regional_segmentation.py
Technical notes: Uses postcode areas to assign UK regions.

What it does: Analyses event names to identify common types of events (e.g. balls, concerts, quiz nights) and how they trend over time.
Output / Recipients: CSVs: keyword_analysis_report*.csv, focused variants
How to run: python3 keyword_analysis_report.py - options: --keywords, --top_n, --industry_filter
Technical notes: Logic in modules/event_keyword_analysis.py.

What it does: Pulls every Mailshake outreach send, matches them against TryBooking accounts, and reports which prospects signed up after being emailed (acquisition attribution).
Output / Recipients: Acquisition report as JSON + CSV; review state stored in app_state.db
How to run: python3 mailshake_acquisition.py - preview without uploading: --dry-run - also save locally: --local-dir out
Technical notes: Reads Mailshake API + Users/Accounts + DuckDB account metrics; reads/writes review decisions+exclusions in SQLite app_state.db. Requires MAILSHAKE_API_KEY. Not on cron.

What it does: Tags users in GetVero after their events complete so they receive automated follow-up messages.
Output / Recipients: Tags applied in GetVero; CSV audit trail saved locally
How to run: python3 event_completion_reminders.py - always test first: export TEST_MODE=1
Technical notes: TEST_MODE skips live Vero writes. API client: modules/utils/vero_api.py.

What it does: Tags users in GetVero who have funds remaining from past events so they can be reminded to use them.
When it runs: PAUSED PROJECT - not scheduled, not currently run
Output / Recipients: Tags applied in GetVero; CSV audit trail saved locally
How to run: python3 funds_remaining_reminder.py - always test first: export TEST_MODE=1
Technical notes: PAUSED PROJECT - kept for reference, may resume. TEST_MODE skips live Vero writes.

What it does: Models what revenue would look like under different fee structures (online, Stripe, box office card), and compares pricing models side by side.
Output / Recipients: CSVs for each scenario saved to output/
How to run: Run scenarios: python3 pricing_scenarios_2026.py (config: pricing_scenarios.yml). Then compare: python3 pricing_model_comparison.py (export YEAR=2025 to choose a year).
Technical notes: Two scripts that work together. pricing_scenarios_2026.py reads 2025 booking data as the baseline (intended to be made generic for future years); pricing_model_comparison.py compares the resulting models.

What it does: Takes a list of account names and fuzzy-matches them against TryBooking data - useful for identifying duplicates, merges, or looking up accounts by partial name.
Output / Recipients: CSV with matched / needs review / no match results
How to run: python3 check_account_names.py - requires a names.txt file in the working directory
Technical notes: Fuzzy matching - handles typos and partial names.

What it does: Ranks every account by Box Office card-present takings over the rolling last 365 days. Spots the biggest box-office clients; can also filter to a single account.
Output / Recipients: box_office_cardpresent_accounts.csv (ranked by fees inc VAT) + top 15 to console
How to run: python3 account_box_office_cardpresent.py - single account: python3 account_box_office_cardpresent.py 19815
Technical notes: Rolling 365 days, Europe/London. Card-present only (Cash excluded). Fees inc VAT. Read-only. Reads BookingData from S3.

What it does: Checks that AWS and Google Analytics credentials are correctly configured before running the PPC report.
Output / Recipients: Console output (pass/fail)
How to run: python3 test_ppc_setup.py
Technical notes: Safe to run at any time - read-only.

What it does: Checks that the Vero API connection is working before running CRM action scripts.
Output / Recipients: Console output (pass/fail)
How to run: python3 test_vero_api.py
Technical notes: Runs in test mode - no live writes.

What it does: Restores the Pi's databases and config from a SharePoint backup - used if the Pi fails or data is lost.
Output / Recipients: Local files restored, decrypted (.env, ecosystem.config.cjs, *.db warehouses)
How to run: python3 restore_from_sharepoint.py --list to see available dates, then --date YYYY-MM-DD
Technical notes: Always run --list first. Prompts for Azure creds (bootstrap) AND the backup passphrase (BACKUP_SECRET_PASSPHRASE, from the password manager) to decrypt - keep it to hand. Restores from backups made by backup_to_sharepoint.py.
